new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record for caom1238 (no catalog record, no existing statement). ch. 2 sections on tone, consonant-tone interaction, tone sandhi) and contains no section headed stress/accent. No verbatim first-hand sentence on word stress was seen; the body text remains unread, so a stress remark inside ch. 2 or ch. 3 cannot be excluded.
new_statements.rule_in_words: From the parts that could be read (author's abstract, publisher's blurb, complete table of contents): Sanjiang Kam is described as a tone language with up to 15 phonetic tones; the phonology chapter is organised around initials, finals, syllable structure, tone, consonant-tone interaction and tone sandhi, and the grammar has no section on word stress or accent. Whether the body text (e.g. 2.4 Syllable structure p. 24, 2.8.2 Variation and change in pronunciation p. 34, 3.4 Disyllabic mono-morphemic words p. 64) makes a passing remark on stress could not be checked because no body text was obtainable; 'has_stress_section: no' rests on the TOC alone.
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes 'Sanjiang Kam', which the author calls 'a less studied southern Kam dialect' spoken by Kam (Dong) people of Meilin village, Sanjiang Dong Autonomous County, Guangxi (author is a native speaker); TOC 1.3.1 is headed 'Why southern Kam dialect of Sanjiang?'. Its assignment to Cao Miao [cov]/caom1238 follows Glottolog's language code 'Sanjiang Kam of Meilin = Grass Miao = Cao Miao [cov]'; the author does not call the variety Cao Miao (草苗话, the Kam lect of the 'Grass Miao' of the Sanshengpo area, Liping/Tongdao/Sanjiang). In ISO terms the variety described is closer to Southern Dong [kmc]; a catalog entry built from this work should carry the label 'Sanjiang Kam (Meilin), southern Kam' and note the Glottolog mapping.

tone_statements.quote: 侗语声调被称为声调演变的活化石。侗语有10个共时调位和15个历史调类。侗语声调由无到有，由少到多，其声调经历了五次漫长的演变过程，侗语应是世界声调语言中声调最多及演变最快的语言。
tone_statements.translation: Kam tones have been called a living fossil of tonal evolution. Kam has 10 synchronic tonemes and 15 historical tone categories. Kam tones went from none to some and from few to many through five long stages of evolution; Kam should be the language with the most tones and the fastest tonal evolution among the world's tone languages.

sources.note: Rich tone systems are a key phonetic trait of Kam-Sui; tone categories correspond fairly completely across Kam-Sui languages, giving a clear thread for reconstructing tone development, while the lects within each language show clear inconsistencies reflecting different developmental stages, which supply the material for reconstructing the Kam-Sui tonal history; second part on how tones behave in Kam song (unseen).

tone.quote: 声调发达,是我国侗水语的一个重要语音特点。侗水语支内部各语言间声调调类有比较完整的对应,为我们研究侗水语声调的发展提供了一条清晰的线索;但各语言的方言土语内部又存在着明显的不一致,各种语言成分的发展状况很不平衡
tone.translation: Well-developed tone systems are an important phonetic feature of the Kam-Sui languages of China. Within the Kam-Sui branch the tone categories of the languages correspond fairly completely, providing a clear thread for studying Kam-Sui tone development; but within the dialects and lects of each language there are clear inconsistencies, the development of the various components being very uneven
tone.summary: Comparative Kam-Sui tone-category correspondences with uneven lect-internal development (details unseen).
tone.says: Rich tone systems are a key phonetic trait of Kam-Sui; tone categories correspond fairly completely across Kam-Sui languages, giving a clear thread for reconstructing tone development, while the lects within each language show clear inconsistencies reflecting different developmental stages, which supply the material for reconstructing the Kam-Sui tonal history; second part on how tones behave in Kam song (unseen).

sources.note: From first-hand Kam lect data the author compares lect phonologies and argues that the North/South dialect boundary should be drawn by presence/absence of the -k coda and that lects should be divided by their tone systems, revising the 1950s classification.

tone.quote: 作者根据自己掌握的第一手侗语方言土语材料,对侗语方言、土语的语音特点进行分析比较,认为划分侗语南北方言的标准是-k韵尾的有无,划分土语的标准是声调,并提出应对50年代方言土语的划分作适当调整。
tone.locator: pp. 50-55 (6 pp); book version = row 100, ch. 侗语语音时空格局分析 §5 侗语方言土语的新划分
tone.translation: On the basis of first-hand Kam dialect and lect materials in his possession the author analyses and compares the phonological features of Kam dialects and lects, holds that the criterion for dividing Northern and Southern Kam is the presence or absence of the -k coda and the criterion for dividing lects is tone, and proposes that the 1950s dialect/lect division be suitably adjusted.
tone.summary: Tone inventories used as the diagnostic for Kam lect division (details unseen).
tone.says: From first-hand Kam lect data the author compares lect phonologies and argues that the North/South dialect boundary should be drawn by presence/absence of the -k coda and that lects should be divided by their tone systems, revising the 1950s classification.

sources.note: Tone is a defining trait of Kam-Tai languages; the Kam tone system is special within the family and informative for the laws of Kam-Tai tone development; the paper gives a general account of Kam tones, especially the constraints initials place on tones, ordering and naming the Kam tone categories after the Chinese four-tone (平上去入 / 阴阳) scheme in line with Tai comparative practice.

tone.quote: 声调是侗泰语族语言的特点之一。声调研究在侗泰语研究中应该占有重要地位。而侗语的声调系统在同语族语言中又有它的特殊之处,对探讨侗泰语声调的发展规律有一定的价值和意义。本文将就侗语的声调,特别是声母对声调的制约关系作概括的阐述。
tone.translation: Tone is one of the characteristics of the Kam-Tai languages. Tone research should hold an important place in Kam-Tai studies. The Kam tone system has its own peculiarities among the languages of the family and is of value for exploring the laws of Kam-Tai tone development. This paper gives a general account of Kam tones, in particular of the constraining relation of initials on tones.
tone.summary: Kam tone categories numbered by the Chinese-style A/B/C/D yin-yang scheme; initial-conditioned distribution of tones (details unseen).
tone.says: Tone is a defining trait of Kam-Tai languages; the Kam tone system is special within the family and informative for the laws of Kam-Tai tone development; the paper gives a general account of Kam tones, especially the constraints initials place on tones, ordering and naming the Kam tone categories after the Chinese four-tone (平上去入 / 阴阳) scheme in line with Tai comparative practice.
